title: Tisus and sfi practice: Swedish test papers · Glossa
description: Timed practice papers for Tisus and the national sfi tests for courses B, C and D, plus a Swedish course to C1. What the tests ask and what the papers leave out.

card.title: Tisus and sfi (Swedish)
card.text: Papers for Tisus, the Swedish test for university studies, and for the national tests of sfi courses B, C and D.

heading: Practise for Tisus and the sfi tests in Swedish.
lead: Two timed practice papers for the reading and writing parts of Tisus, the test that shows your Swedish is good enough for studies at a Swedish university. Behind them is a complete Swedish course to C1, with the academic and formal Swedish the test is built on. There are also two papers each for the national tests of sfi (svenska för invandrare) courses B, C and D, in their reading, listening and writing formats.
fineprint: The Swedish course is free. The practice papers are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year. Also available for Finnish, Russian, Ukrainian, Norwegian and Danish speakers.

panel.label: From practice paper 1, reading
panel.title: Föreläsningssalen behövs fortfarande
panel.text: Under pandemiåren lärde sig svenska lärosäten att undervisa på distans på rekordtid. Föreläsningar spelades in, seminarier flyttade till videomöten och tentamina skrevs hemma vid köksbordet.
panel.question: Vilken är författarens huvudsakliga ståndpunkt?
options: Inspelade föreläsningar bör inte längre få användas vid universiteten.
Undervisning där studenterna möts bör inte helt ersättas av inspelningar.
Lärosätena bör återgå till den undervisning som fanns före pandemin.

sections.heading: What Tisus asks
sections.intro: Tisus (Test i svenska för universitets- och högskolestudier) is run by Stockholm University. Its level matches the upper-secondary courses Svenska 3 and Svenska som andraspråk 3; Stockholm University does not tie it to a CEFR level, although others often describe it as C1. There is no listening part. Reading and writing are taken on the same morning, and speaking the same or the next day.
rows: 75 minutes. First 30 questions on five texts of 500 to 900 words, such as opinion pieces, editorials and popular science: multiple choice with three options, statements that are or are not supported by the text, and a few short answers. Then 15 search questions on one long text, such as a report, answered in a few words from the text. No aids.
The same task types, with three texts of five questions each and one long text to search. 40 minutes.

2 hours 30 minutes. One argumentative text (resonerande text) of about 400 words with a given title, for an educated general reader, with a short background text and optional quotations. A Swedish–Swedish dictionary is allowed.
The full task and the full 2 hours 30 minutes, rated by AI against the Tisus criteria.
About 30 minutes. In Sweden, a group discussion of about 20 minutes on a topic sent a week before and a short individual talk; abroad, a recorded monologue of 10 to 15 minutes.
Not included: Glossa cannot yet assess free speech.
sections.note: Based on Stockholm University's published descriptions of Tisus, checked in October 2026.

sections.heading: How Tisus is graded
sections.intro: Each part is graded godkänd (pass) or underkänd (fail), and you need a pass in all three.
items: The reading pass mark is set after each test and is usually around 24 to 30 of 45 points.
If you fail one part, you retake only that part within a year; if you fail two or three, you retake the whole test.

sections.heading: The national tests of sfi courses B, C and D
intro: Sfi (svenska för invandrare, Swedish for immigrants) is the Swedish course of municipal adult education (komvux). Skolverket is responsible for its national tests (nationella prov) for courses B, C and D, which a group at Stockholm University develops with Skolverket; course A has none.

These are not tests you can book. Students enrolled in sfi take them at their school near the end of the course, and their teacher gives and marks them. The result is one of the things the teacher weighs when setting the course grade, Godkänt (pass) or Icke godkänt (fail). The tests stay confidential, so Glossa's papers practise their formats; they are not the tests. Each test has reading, listening, writing and speaking, with vocabulary and grammar part of every task, and Skolverket estimates the whole test at four to five hours.
rows: Listening and reading on short, clear texts (about 25 and 35 sub-items), one narrative text about yourself or something you have experienced, and a conversation with your teacher.
15 listening and 20 reading questions and the full writing task, in 20, 35 and 30 minutes. No speaking.
Reading in two booklets (about 40 questions), listening (24 questions), one more informal text such as an e-mail to a friend, and speaking alone and in pairs.
About 22 reading and 14 listening questions and one writing task, in 40, 20 and 40 minutes. No speaking.
Reading longer texts in two booklets (about 38 sub-items), listening (24 sub-items), two texts, one informal and one more formal, and speaking alone and in pairs.
About 22 reading and 14 listening questions and both writing tasks, in 45, 25 and 90 minutes. No speaking.
sections.note: Based on Skolverket's descriptions of the national tests, checked in November 2026. The time limits of the real parts are in the teachers' instructions, which are not public, so Glossa's times are its own. New sfi course plans apply to studies started after 31 December 2026, with a new series of national tests from 18 January 2027; Skolverket has not said that the parts change.

sections.heading: What citizenship asks of your Swedish
sections.intro: Since 6 June 2026, applicants for Swedish citizenship aged 16 to 66 must show knowledge of Swedish. Migrationsverket asks for reading and listening at B1 and speaking and writing at A2, and accepts, among other proofs:
items: a pass grade in sfi course D, the highest sfi course. What counts is the course grade, not the national test on its own; a pass in course B or C does not meet the requirement;
other school grades in Swedish. Migrationsverket decides on citizenship and sets the other conditions.

sections.heading: Papers to practise on, and a course to learn from

items.title: Two papers for each test
items.text: Two for Tisus, on topics such as recorded lectures, closing village schools, a shorter working week and disappearing cash, and two each for sfi courses B, C and D, on everyday life, society, studies and work in Sweden. All with original texts and a writing task.

items.title: Writing rated against the criteria
items.text: Your argumentative text is rated by AI against the Tisus criteria, with what to improve. It is an estimate, not an assessor's grade.

items.title: A full course behind the papers
items.text: 75 modules in eight tiers to C1. Tiers 7 and 8 cover nominal style, connectors, word formation, the Swedish of the authorities, register and style, and academic Swedish, so a weak spot in a paper has a module to go back to.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer in the course gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule. Every Swedish word can be tapped for its forms, meaning and audio.

sections.heading: How the practice papers differ from the real test
items: Reading and listening are shorter, with fewer texts and questions than the real tests. Writing is full length.
There is no speaking part, neither the Tisus discussion nor the sfi conversation with your teacher.

No pass mark is shown. The real Tisus reading pass mark changes from test to test, and the sfi cut scores are not published, so a paper shows the share of points only and cannot tell you whether you would pass.
The writing score is an AI estimate against the Tisus criteria or the sfi assessment matrix, not an assessor's or teacher's grade.

items.question: Is Glossa an official Tisus or sfi preparation course?
items.answer: No. Glossa is not connected with Stockholm University or Skolverket. The papers follow their published descriptions of the tests, with original content.

items.question: Can I book the sfi test?
items.answer: No. The national sfi tests are taken only by students enrolled in sfi, at their school, near the end of each course. Glossa's sfi papers help you practise the formats alongside the course.

items.question: Is there a listening part?
items.answer: No. Tisus has reading, writing and speaking. Glossa's papers cover reading and writing.

items.question: What is free?
items.answer: The whole Swedish course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference and word practice are free. The Tisus and sfi practice papers, the specializations, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.

items.question: I speak Finnish. Is there a course for me?
items.answer: Yes. Swedish for Finnish speakers has the same Tisus and sfi papers with the instructions in Finnish, and also papers for the Swedish YKI test at the intermediate level.

items.question: I speak Russian, Ukrainian, Norwegian or Danish. Is there a course for me?
items.answer: Yes. Swedish for Russian speakers and Swedish for Ukrainian speakers have the same Tisus and sfi papers, with the instructions in Russian or Ukrainian. Swedish for Danish speakers, a shorter course, has the Tisus and sfi papers too, and Swedish for Norwegian speakers the Tisus papers.

closing.heading: Start with the course, practise with the papers.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Swedish, and open the first module or the practice papers.

trademark: Tisus (Test i svenska för universitets- och högskolestudier) is run by Stockholm University. Skolverket is responsible for the national sfi tests. Glossa is not affiliated with or endorsed by either.
